title: implement dense sidebar diagnostic panels for Magic Context
description:
## Program goal

Deliver an opt-in Dense Collapsed Sidebar and focused diagnostic subpanel system for Magic Context's OpenCode TUI sidebar.

The work preserves the current Classic collapsed mode as the initial default, adds a superior dense mode for power users, and reorganizes expanded diagnostic information into focused panels rather than a single cluttered report.

## Source references

- Final PRD artifact: magic-context-dense-sidebar-prd.md (generated from design phase on 2026-06-13).
- Target repository: cortexkit/magic-context, current main plus new feature branch from Zireael/magic-context.
- Prior closed PR context: cortexkit/magic-context#93 and branch `Zireael/magic-context:feat/sidebar-collapse`.
- Current upstream behavior: main branch already implements a basic collapsible sidebar, but it does not persist collapse state, remains too verbose, and lacks dense context/cache telemetry.

## Context summary

The final PRD defines a dense 3-4 line instrument strip:

```text
180K · HIST↻ · Q3
████▒▒|░░      61%
⡀⣇⡄⣇⡆⡇⣇⣧⣷⣿   92.6%
[D] [S] [A] [F]3
```

It also defines focused subpanels:

```text
[Overview] [Alloc] [Memory]
[Tokens] [Cache] [Settings]
[X Close]
```

The panel must not lie about token totals after Magic Context flushes, prunes, or compacts messages. Historical token usage must come from durable provider/OpenCode usage events, while current context pressure may use Magic Context's snapshot estimates.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Classic collapsed remains available and remains default until intentionally changed.
- [ ] Dense collapsed mode can be selected, persisted, reset to config default, and rendered across supported widths.
- [ ] Dense strip displays model context capacity, context pressure, threshold/overflow markers, stability-density segments, risk/process state, optional cache row, and stable action order.
- [ ] `[F]n` appears last only when flushable work exists.
- [ ] Details, Status/Allocation, Mode/Automation, Memory, Tokens, Cache, and Settings panels are reachable and close with `[X Close]`.
- [ ] Token panel separates exact provider usage ledger from current visible context estimates.
- [ ] Settings panel shows Magic Context version and update status.
- [ ] Critical blinking/inversion is limited to real active faults, not decorative volatile segments.
- [ ] Unit, integration, and visual fixture coverage exists for healthy, fresh, pressure, cache-critical, Historian-running, overflow, no-cache, and cold-context states.
- [ ] Independent verification Bead completes with acceptance mapping and evidence.

## Non-goals

- Do not remove or regress Classic collapsed mode.
- Do not make Dense mode the default in this work package.
- Do not fabricate cache, token, or eviction precision when telemetry is unavailable.
- Do not make Nerd Fonts required.
- Do not rely on summing visible messages for historical token accounting after pruning/compaction.

## Child Bead plan

Recommended sequential implementation order:

1. `mc-sidp-01-audit`
2. `mc-sidp-02-display-mode`
3. `mc-sidp-03-dense-strip`
4. `mc-sidp-04-risk-classifier`
5. `mc-sidp-05-panel-shell`
6. `mc-sidp-06-core-panels`
7. `mc-sidp-07-memory-panel`
8. `mc-sidp-08-cache-telemetry`
9. `mc-sidp-09-token-ledger`
10. `mc-sidp-10-settings-version`
11. `mc-sidp-11-glyph-alerts`
12. `mc-sidp-12-tests-fixtures`
13. `mc-sidp-13-docs`
14. `mc-sidp-14-verification`
15. `mc-sidp-15-milestone`

## Validation strategy

- Run repo's TypeScript/build/test/lint commands discovered during `mc-sidp-01-audit`.
- Add unit tests for derived UI state helpers and pure render helpers.
- Add fixture/snapshot tests for dense strip and subpanels where the project test stack supports it.
- Verify token ledger behavior with a pruning/compaction simulation.
- Verify no cache row renders when cache telemetry is absent or stale.
- Verify Classic collapsed mode remains unchanged unless the user explicitly opts into Dense mode.

## Prior-art handling

Implementation should start from latest `cortexkit/magic-context:master`. PR #93 is closed and stale relative to master, but its source is valuable prior art. The coding agent must harvest concrete patterns from PR #93 during `mc-sidp-01-audit` and then implement against current master.
## Theme/palette/motion extension added 2026-06-13

Additional child beads `mc-sidp-16` through `mc-sidp-22` extend the original dense sidebar plan with:

- OpenCode theme token integration through `api.theme.current`;
- semantic sidebar palette adapter;
- curated reduced OpenCode-derived packaged palettes;
- per-semantic-token color overrides;
- Settings UI for theme source, preset, and overrides;
- reduced-motion-aware pulse policy as a subtler alternative to blinking;
- focused test coverage for theme, override, and motion behavior.

These beads are inserted after `mc-sidp-11-glyph-alerts` and before global `mc-sidp-12-tests-fixtures`, so the final test/docs/verification pass covers the complete UI design.

## Theme/palette/motion extension success criteria

- Dense/sidebar rendering can follow OpenCode's active theme through `api.theme.current`.
- Users can select Magic Context-local Magic Default, packaged preset, Monochrome, and High Contrast theme sources.
- Users can override every Magic Context sidebar semantic color token individually.
- Packaged presets use reduced sidebar palette mappings only and preserve OpenCode MIT attribution if derived from OpenCode defaults.
- Motion policy supports subtle, reduced, and off modes; pulse is used only as a severity/attention channel and never as decoration.
- All final verification includes theme, override, and motion behavior.

title: audit OpenCode theme API and palette integration seams
description:
## Source references

- Existing root epic: `mc-sidp-epic`.
- Existing final PRD: `magic-context-dense-sidebar-prd.md`.
- Updated Beads base: `mc-sidp-beads.v2-pr93-salvage.jsonl`.
- OpenCode source review findings:
  - TUI plugins receive `props.api.theme.current` through `TuiPluginApi.theme`.
  - `api.theme.current` exposes resolved theme tokens including text, muted text, selected item text, backgrounds, border, success, warning, error, info, accent, diff, markdown, syntax, and `thinkingOpacity`.
  - `api.theme.selected`, `api.theme.has(name)`, `api.theme.set(name)`, `api.theme.install(jsonPath)`, `api.theme.mode()`, and `api.theme.ready` are exposed.
  - Public plugin API does not appear to expose a full `theme.list()` / `theme.all()` method, even though OpenCode internal TUI theme picker can list all themes.
  - Built-in OpenCode TUI sidebar plugins already use `props.api.theme.current` directly.
- OpenCode default theme source review findings:
  - OpenCode imports default theme JSON assets and collects them into `DEFAULT_THEMES`.
  - Defaults include themes such as `opencode`, `nord`, `gruvbox`, `catppuccin`, `tokyonight`, `github`, `dracula`, `kanagawa`, `ayu`, `aura`, `vercel`, `zenburn`, and others.
  - OpenCode theme JSON includes many fields Magic Context should not expose directly: markdown, syntax, diff, background-menu, and other unrelated tokens.
- License note:
  - OpenCode is MIT licensed. If Magic Context copies reduced color mappings derived from OpenCode default theme files, preserve attribution/copyright/license notice in source comments or documentation.

## Objective

Perform a focused implementation audit for theme, palette, and motion integration before coding the theme system.

The purpose is to prevent the implementation agent from re-researching OpenCode theme internals during later beads and to capture exact current-code seams in Magic Context and OpenCode.

## Current behavior

Magic Context dense sidebar planning already includes glyphs, alerts, settings, and optional theme following. OpenCode exposes current theme tokens to TUI plugins, but Magic Context still needs a local semantic palette layer, packaged reduced presets, per-token overrides, and motion policy.

## Desired behavior

After this audit, later beads should know exactly:

- where Magic Context currently renders sidebar styles;
- whether current code has an existing theme abstraction or hardcoded colors;
- where OpenCode TUI plugin `api.theme.current` enters Magic Context code;
- what token names/types are available from current OpenCode API;
- whether theme changes are reactive while the sidebar is mounted;
- what terminal renderer supports for foreground, background, opacity/dimming, inverse, and animation/timers;
- which OpenCode default themes should be packaged as reduced Magic Context sidebar presets;
- what license/attribution file or source comment must be added if reduced OpenCode mappings are copied.

## Scope

- Inspect source only.
- Produce implementation notes in the bead handoff.
- Make no production behavior changes unless trivial tests/docs are needed to record findings.

## Out of scope

- Do not implement theme mode selection.
- Do not vendor or generate palettes yet.
- Do not add runtime settings UI yet.
- Do not change user-visible sidebar colors yet.
design:
## Implementation / investigation plan

1. Inspect Magic Context current sidebar rendering files:
   - sidebar content/root component;
   - dense/classic collapsed components if already added by earlier beads;
   - sidebar utility/helper files;
   - settings panel code if present;
   - config schema/parser.
2. Inspect OpenCode TUI plugin API usage from Magic Context:
   - locate `props.api` / `TuiPluginApi` use;
   - confirm the exact type/path for `api.theme.current` and `api.theme.selected` in the installed dependency or workspace.
3. Inspect OpenCode theme source assets:
   - locate imported default themes;
   - list all defaults, but recommend a curated subset for Magic Context packaging.
4. Confirm whether OpenCode public plugin API exposes a theme list:
   - if no public list exists, record that Magic Context must not promise a full OpenCode theme picker;
   - allow packaged presets and typed validated OpenCode theme name using `api.theme.has(name)` if useful.
5. Inspect terminal/TUI rendering capabilities:
   - foreground/background colors;
   - alpha/opacity support if any;
   - dim/inverse/bold;
   - timer/interval support for pulse motion;
   - testability of animation through injected clock/phase.
6. Inspect current project test conventions and identify the test files that should cover theme resolution and settings UI.
7. Decide curated packaged preset list. Default recommendation:
   - `opencode`, `nord`, `gruvbox`, `catppuccin`, `tokyonight`, `github`, plus Magic Context `monochrome`, `highContrast`, and `magicDefault`.
8. Write handoff notes with file paths, APIs, constraints, and any drift from this bead.

## Mandatory code reading before closing

- Magic Context sidebar renderer files.
- Magic Context config/schema files.
- Magic Context test setup for sidebar/config rendering.
- OpenCode TUI plugin API type definitions in the installed/current source.
- OpenCode built-in sidebar plugin examples that use `props.api.theme.current`.
- OpenCode default theme asset index and resolver if accessible.
- OpenCode LICENSE or package license metadata if copying reduced mappings is planned.

## Discovered-work protocol

If the audit finds no usable `api.theme.current` access in Magic Context's runtime context, create a blocker bead for plugin API wiring before closing this audit as complete.

If OpenCode theme token shapes have changed, update later beads or create a discovered bead that documents the new source of truth.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance criteria

- Handoff identifies the exact Magic Context files to modify for theme palette resolution and Settings UI integration.
- Handoff identifies the exact OpenCode TUI plugin API source/type that exposes current theme tokens.
- Handoff explicitly states whether full OpenCode theme listing is available to plugins. If unavailable, later beads must not require full theme list selection.
- Handoff records a curated packaged preset list or explains why packaging presets should be deferred.
- Handoff records license/attribution requirements for reduced OpenCode-derived palette mappings.
- Handoff records terminal rendering capabilities for color, background, dim/inverse, opacity, and pulse animation.
- Handoff records test files or test harnesses to use for later implementation beads.

## Validation commands

- `bd show mc-sidp-epic --json`

- Inspect `package.json` scripts and run the narrowest relevant static/type check if available.

## Handoff requirements

Close with:

- source paths inspected;
- API facts confirmed;
- curated preset recommendation;
- license note;
- implementation risks;
- next bead recommendation.

title: implement semantic sidebar theme adapter
description:
## Source references

- Existing root epic: `mc-sidp-epic`.
- Existing final PRD: `magic-context-dense-sidebar-prd.md`.
- Updated Beads base: `mc-sidp-beads.v2-pr93-salvage.jsonl`.
- OpenCode source review findings:
  - TUI plugins receive `props.api.theme.current` through `TuiPluginApi.theme`.
  - `api.theme.current` exposes resolved theme tokens including text, muted text, selected item text, backgrounds, border, success, warning, error, info, accent, diff, markdown, syntax, and `thinkingOpacity`.
  - `api.theme.selected`, `api.theme.has(name)`, `api.theme.set(name)`, `api.theme.install(jsonPath)`, `api.theme.mode()`, and `api.theme.ready` are exposed.
  - Public plugin API does not appear to expose a full `theme.list()` / `theme.all()` method, even though OpenCode internal TUI theme picker can list all themes.
  - Built-in OpenCode TUI sidebar plugins already use `props.api.theme.current` directly.
- OpenCode default theme source review findings:
  - OpenCode imports default theme JSON assets and collects them into `DEFAULT_THEMES`.
  - Defaults include themes such as `opencode`, `nord`, `gruvbox`, `catppuccin`, `tokyonight`, `github`, `dracula`, `kanagawa`, `ayu`, `aura`, `vercel`, `zenburn`, and others.
  - OpenCode theme JSON includes many fields Magic Context should not expose directly: markdown, syntax, diff, background-menu, and other unrelated tokens.
- License note:
  - OpenCode is MIT licensed. If Magic Context copies reduced color mappings derived from OpenCode default theme files, preserve attribution/copyright/license notice in source comments or documentation.

## Objective

Implement a semantic theme adapter for the Magic Context sidebar so all dense-sidebar colors are selected by purpose rather than hardcoded raw color names.

This bead is the foundation for Follow OpenCode, Magic Default, Monochrome, High Contrast, packaged presets, per-color overrides, and motion/pulse styling.

## Current behavior

The dense sidebar design needs semantic colors for context pressure, cache state, risk flags, selected tabs, panels, and motion/pulse states. Without a central adapter, later implementation would scatter hardcoded colors across components and make theme following/overrides brittle.

## Desired behavior

Magic Context should resolve a `MagicSidebarPalette` from the active theme source and expose semantic style helpers to sidebar components.

Required base theme sources:

```ts
type SidebarThemeSource =
  | "follow_opencode"
  | "magic_default"
  | "packaged_preset"
  | "monochrome"
  | "high_contrast"
```

This bead should implement `follow_opencode`, `magic_default`, `monochrome`, and `high_contrast`. `packaged_preset` may initially route to `magic_default` or a placeholder until `mc-sidp-18-packaged-palettes` implements real presets.

## Required semantic tokens

```ts
type SidebarColorToken =
  | "text"
  | "textMuted"
  | "border"
  | "panel"
  | "selectedFg"
  | "selectedBg"
  | "ok"
  | "info"
  | "warning"
  | "critical"
  | "cold"
  | "warm"
  | "hot"
  | "free"
  | "threshold"
  | "overflow"
  | "cacheGood"
  | "cacheDegraded"
  | "cacheBad"
  | "pulseActive"
  | "pulseWarning"
  | "pulseCritical"
```

## Scope

- Add semantic palette types.
- Add palette resolver.
- Add `fromOpenCodeTheme(api.theme.current)` mapping.
- Add Magic Default, Monochrome, and High Contrast palettes.
- Add rendering helpers so components call semantic colors, not raw color strings.
- Wire existing dense/sidebar rendering to the adapter where feasible.

## Out of scope

- Do not package reduced OpenCode presets yet except minimal placeholders if necessary.
- Do not implement per-token user overrides yet.
- Do not build Settings UI for theme editing yet.
- Do not implement pulse animation yet.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance criteria

- A central semantic sidebar theme module exists and is used by dense/sidebar components touched by this work.
- `follow_opencode` mode resolves from `api.theme.current` without importing OpenCode internal theme assets.
- `magic_default`, `monochrome`, and `high_contrast` palettes are implemented.
- Raw color strings are not scattered in dense-sidebar render code for semantic states; components use the adapter/helper.
- Color is not the only indicator for warnings/errors; `T!`, `C!`, `H!`, `>`, `|`, and glyph density remain meaningful without color.
- Fallback behavior prevents sidebar render failure when theme API is unavailable or incomplete.
- Unit tests cover palette resolution for at least Follow OpenCode, Monochrome, High Contrast, invalid source fallback, and missing token fallback.

## Validation commands

- Inspect `package.json` scripts first.
- Run relevant unit tests for sidebar theme adapter.
- Run typecheck/lint if available.
- Run existing sidebar tests to ensure no renderer regression.

## Handoff requirements

Close with:

- files changed;
- semantic tokens implemented;
- mapping decisions from OpenCode tokens to Magic Context tokens;
- validation commands/results;
- any deferred mappings or discovered palette gaps.

## Handoff notes

No implementation notes yet. Update this section when claiming or closing the bead.

title: package reduced OpenCode-derived sidebar palettes
description:
## Source references

- Existing root epic: `mc-sidp-epic`.
- Existing final PRD: `magic-context-dense-sidebar-prd.md`.
- Updated Beads base: `mc-sidp-beads.v2-pr93-salvage.jsonl`.
- OpenCode source review findings:
  - TUI plugins receive `props.api.theme.current` through `TuiPluginApi.theme`.
  - `api.theme.current` exposes resolved theme tokens including text, muted text, selected item text, backgrounds, border, success, warning, error, info, accent, diff, markdown, syntax, and `thinkingOpacity`.
  - `api.theme.selected`, `api.theme.has(name)`, `api.theme.set(name)`, `api.theme.install(jsonPath)`, `api.theme.mode()`, and `api.theme.ready` are exposed.
  - Public plugin API does not appear to expose a full `theme.list()` / `theme.all()` method, even though OpenCode internal TUI theme picker can list all themes.
  - Built-in OpenCode TUI sidebar plugins already use `props.api.theme.current` directly.
- OpenCode default theme source review findings:
  - OpenCode imports default theme JSON assets and collects them into `DEFAULT_THEMES`.
  - Defaults include themes such as `opencode`, `nord`, `gruvbox`, `catppuccin`, `tokyonight`, `github`, `dracula`, `kanagawa`, `ayu`, `aura`, `vercel`, `zenburn`, and others.
  - OpenCode theme JSON includes many fields Magic Context should not expose directly: markdown, syntax, diff, background-menu, and other unrelated tokens.
- License note:
  - OpenCode is MIT licensed. If Magic Context copies reduced color mappings derived from OpenCode default theme files, preserve attribution/copyright/license notice in source comments or documentation.

## Objective

Package a curated set of reduced Magic Context sidebar palettes derived from OpenCode default themes, without vendoring full OpenCode theme files or exposing unrelated theme tokens.

## Current behavior

Follow OpenCode can use the active runtime theme, but users may want Magic Context to use a stable palette independent of the active OpenCode theme. OpenCode's default theme set is larger and contains many tokens irrelevant to Magic Context.

## Desired behavior

Magic Context should include a small curated set of packaged sidebar palettes:

Recommended initial set:

```text
opencode
nord
gruvbox
catppuccin
tokyonight
github
magicDefault
monochrome
highContrast
```

Optionally include `dracula` and `kanagawa` if extraction is cheap and test coverage stays manageable.

Each packaged preset should define only `MagicSidebarPalette` semantic tokens. Do not copy entire OpenCode theme JSON.

## Scope

- Add a packaged preset registry.
- Add reduced semantic mappings for curated presets.
- Add source/license attribution for any mappings derived from OpenCode default theme files.
- Ensure unknown preset names fall back safely.
- Expose preset metadata needed by Settings UI.

## Out of scope

- Do not implement a full OpenCode theme browser.
- Do not expose raw OpenCode markdown/syntax/diff tokens.
- Do not build an upstream sync pipeline unless it is very small and non-disruptive.
- Do not import OpenCode internal default theme JSON at runtime unless current repository architecture makes that clearly safe.
design:
## Implementation plan

1. Use `mc-sidp-16-theme-audit` findings to locate OpenCode default theme assets and license requirements.
2. Create a reduced palette registry, for example:

```ts
const packagedSidebarPalettes: Record<string, MagicSidebarPalette> = {
  opencode: { ... },
  nord: { ... },
  gruvbox: { ... },
  catppuccin: { ... },
  tokyonight: { ... },
  github: { ... },
  magicDefault: { ... },
  monochrome: { ... },
  highContrast: { ... },
}
```

3. If OpenCode theme tokens use references or dark/light variants, resolve them manually or with a small extraction helper. Do not copy unresolved references into Magic Context palette objects unless the resolver supports them.
4. Implement `getPackagedSidebarPalette(name)` and `listPackagedSidebarPalettes()`.
5. Ensure `packaged_preset` source in `resolveSidebarPalette` works with configured preset name.
6. Add attribution:
   - source comment near palette definitions; and/or
   - documentation/license note in Magic Context docs;
   - retain MIT attribution for copied/reduced OpenCode mappings.
7. Keep semantic mapping purposeful:
   - `cold`: stable/cool color;
   - `warm`: amber/yellow/mid-attention;
   - `hot`: orange/red/high attention;
   - `free`: dim/muted;
   - cache good/degraded/bad should follow green/yellow/red or theme-appropriate equivalents.
8. Avoid copying everything from OpenCode. If a color cannot be derived sensibly, use the Magic Default semantic value or a theme-appropriate fallback.

## Optional generator guidance

A generator is allowed only if it remains small and deterministic:

```text
scripts/extract-opencode-sidebar-palettes.ts
```

It may read OpenCode theme JSON assets and emit reduced semantic palettes. If added, the generated file must include a source warning and tests must not require network access.

Do not make the generator required for normal build unless the project already supports generated files cleanly.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance criteria

- `packaged_preset` theme source resolves named reduced sidebar palettes.
- Curated presets include at minimum: `opencode`, `nord`, `gruvbox`, `catppuccin`, `tokyonight`, `github`, `magicDefault`, `monochrome`, and `highContrast`, unless the bead handoff explicitly justifies a smaller set.
- Packaged presets contain only Magic Context semantic sidebar tokens, not full OpenCode theme JSON.
- Unknown preset name falls back safely and does not crash rendering.
- Source/license attribution is present for mappings derived from OpenCode defaults.
- Tests verify preset lookup, fallback, and that each packaged palette has all required semantic tokens.
- Tests or snapshots verify that Monochrome and High Contrast remain distinguishable from normal color presets.

## Validation commands

- Run palette registry unit tests.
- Run typecheck/lint if available.
- Run any license/header test if repository has one.
- Manually inspect built package or source tree to confirm full OpenCode theme JSON files were not unnecessarily vendored.

## Handoff requirements

Close with:

- list of packaged presets;
- source/attribution location;
- whether generator was added or manually curated;
- validation commands/results;
- any additional presets proposed as deferred follow-up beads.

No implementation notes yet. Update this section when claiming or closing the bead.

title: add per-token sidebar color override configuration
description:
## Source references

- Existing root epic: `mc-sidp-epic`.
- Existing final PRD: `magic-context-dense-sidebar-prd.md`.
- Updated Beads base: `mc-sidp-beads.v2-pr93-salvage.jsonl`.
- OpenCode source review findings:
  - TUI plugins receive `props.api.theme.current` through `TuiPluginApi.theme`.
  - `api.theme.current` exposes resolved theme tokens including text, muted text, selected item text, backgrounds, border, success, warning, error, info, accent, diff, markdown, syntax, and `thinkingOpacity`.
  - `api.theme.selected`, `api.theme.has(name)`, `api.theme.set(name)`, `api.theme.install(jsonPath)`, `api.theme.mode()`, and `api.theme.ready` are exposed.
  - Public plugin API does not appear to expose a full `theme.list()` / `theme.all()` method, even though OpenCode internal TUI theme picker can list all themes.
  - Built-in OpenCode TUI sidebar plugins already use `props.api.theme.current` directly.
- OpenCode default theme source review findings:
  - OpenCode imports default theme JSON assets and collects them into `DEFAULT_THEMES`.
  - Defaults include themes such as `opencode`, `nord`, `gruvbox`, `catppuccin`, `tokyonight`, `github`, `dracula`, `kanagawa`, `ayu`, `aura`, `vercel`, `zenburn`, and others.
  - OpenCode theme JSON includes many fields Magic Context should not expose directly: markdown, syntax, diff, background-menu, and other unrelated tokens.
- License note:
  - OpenCode is MIT licensed. If Magic Context copies reduced color mappings derived from OpenCode default theme files, preserve attribution/copyright/license notice in source comments or documentation.

## Objective

Allow users to override every Magic Context sidebar semantic color individually, while preserving a safe fallback to the selected base theme source.

## Current behavior

The theme adapter can resolve semantic palettes from Follow OpenCode, Magic Default, Monochrome, High Contrast, and packaged presets. Users still need precise control over individual semantic colors such as `warning`, `critical`, `cold`, `hot`, and `cacheDegraded`.

## Desired behavior

Users can set per-token overrides in config and later through Settings UI.

Config shape:

```jsonc
{
  "tui": {
    "sidebar": {
      "theme": {
        "source": "follow_opencode",
        "preset": "opencode",
        "overrides": {
          "warning": "#d79921",
          "cold": "#7aa2f7"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Override resolution:

```text
base palette from theme source
  -> apply semantic token overrides
  -> validated final palette
```

description:

- Existing final PRD: `magic-context-dense-sidebar-prd.md`.

- OpenCode source review findings:
  - TUI plugins receive `props.api.theme.current` through `TuiPluginApi.theme`.
  - `api.theme.current` exposes resolved theme tokens including text, muted text, selected item text, backgrounds, border, success, warning, error, info, accent, diff, markdown, syntax, and `thinkingOpacity`.
  - `api.theme.selected`, `api.theme.has(name)`, `api.theme.set(name)`, `api.theme.install(jsonPath)`, `api.theme.mode()`, and `api.theme.ready` are exposed.
  - Public plugin API does not appear to expose a full `theme.list()` / `theme.all()` method, even though OpenCode internal TUI theme picker can list all themes.
  - Built-in OpenCode TUI sidebar plugins already use `props.api.theme.current` directly.
- OpenCode default theme source review findings:
  - OpenCode imports default theme JSON assets and collects them into `DEFAULT_THEMES`.
  - Defaults include themes such as `opencode`, `nord`, `gruvbox`, `catppuccin`, `tokyonight`, `github`, `dracula`, `kanagawa`, `ayu`, `aura`, `vercel`, `zenburn`, and others.
  - OpenCode theme JSON includes many fields Magic Context should not expose directly: markdown, syntax, diff, background-menu, and other unrelated tokens.
- License note:
  - OpenCode is MIT licensed. If Magic Context copies reduced color mappings derived from OpenCode default theme files, preserve attribution/copyright/license notice in source comments or documentation.

## Objective

Implement a reduced-motion-aware pulse/severity styling policy for the dense sidebar that provides subtler alternatives to blinking while preserving clear critical alerts.

## Current behavior

The dense sidebar design uses static colors and rare critical blink/invert. The user requested slower fading/pulsing color or opacity changes as a subtler alternative to blinking.

## Desired behavior

Motion should be a controlled severity channel, not decoration.

Escalation model:

```text
static color       = normal status
slow pulse         = active process or soft warning
strong pulse       = degraded / act soon
blink / hard invert = critical / act now, only if enabled
```

Motion modes:

```ts
type SidebarMotionMode = "subtle" | "reduced" | "off"
```

Default recommendation:

```text
theme = follow_opencode
motion = subtle
```

## Scope

- Add motion config/state.
- Implement pulse style resolver using semantic tokens from `MagicSidebarPalette`.
- Apply pulse only to the smallest meaningful UI token/chip/label, not whole rows/bars.
- Respect `motion = reduced` and `motion = off`.
- Preserve critical no-motion fallback using static flags/inverse styling.

## Out of scope

- Do not animate every glyph independently.
- Do not add per-glyph animation controls.
- Do not implement decorative blinking.
- Do not make hot tool-call segments pulse merely because they are hot.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance criteria

- Motion config supports `subtle`, `reduced`, and `off`.
- Pulse styling is routed through semantic theme tokens, not hardcoded raw colors.
- Soft pulse applies only to approved active/soft-warning elements.
- Strong pulse applies only to degraded/act-soon elements.
- Blink/invert remains reserved for critical states and respects existing critical-alert policy.
- `motion = off` disables all animation and preserves meaning with static glyphs/text/styles.
- Tests cover pulse target selection, reduced/off behavior, deterministic phase rendering, and critical fallback.
- No allocation category row or normal hot segment pulses merely because it is hot.

## Validation commands

- Run motion policy unit tests.
- Run dense strip snapshot tests in motion-off and at fixed pulse phases.
- Run Settings panel tests for Motion controls.
- Run typecheck/lint if available.

## Handoff requirements

Close with:

- implemented motion modes;
- list of pulse targets;
- tests added;
- validation commands/results;
- any terminal limitations discovered.
